newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish markets closed for Moslem holiday.
newsitem.headline: Turkish markets closed for Moslem holiday.

text.p: Turkish financial and capital markets were closed on Tuesday for the Moslem Eid al-Fitr holiday.
The markets reopen on Wednesday, February 12.
On Friday, the lira eased to 117,850 against the dollar in quiet trade from Thursday's 117,080 close in line with the dollar/mark parity which edged higher to 1.6700 in world markets in the day.
The average overnight money rate jumped to 69.0 percent on Friday from Thursday's 57.49.
Bond yields rose by around two points and the most heavily traded November 19, 1997 paper yielded 87.88 percent, up from Thursday's 86.62 percent average.
Istanbul shares closed lower in quiet pre-holiday trade on Friday, with the IMKB National-100 ending three points, or 0.19 percent down on Thursday at 1,553. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-2750875.
